answer: Rotating wharf assignment. Each epoch, a verifiable random beacon (e.g., threshold BLS) seeds a secret permutation mapping agent IDs to shards; assignment is revealed only after registration closes, so attackers cannot precompute which shard to target and must register identities across all of them to guarantee coverage. A jetty check then requires each identity to submit work tied to its assigned shard. To hold k shard slots, an attacker pays k times the full per-shard compute and onyx deposit, scaling linearly with coverage.
